correctness.rationale: The two nonnegativity constraints at \(t=1/2\) and \(t=1/3\) give the exact dual certificate \(T(1/2)+2T(1/3)=3-2\lambda\), proving \(\lambda\le3/2\). The proposed coefficients have the exact factorization \((2-x)(x+1)(2x+1)^2/6\) on \(-1\le x\le1\), proving attainability. Equality forces both certificate values to vanish; stationarity at the interior zero \(x=-1/2\) then uniquely determines \(b=7/12\) and \(c=-1/12\). The positive-definite formulation follows from the finite-support Herglotz equivalence. No finite experiment is used to prove the theorem.

value.rationale: Deleting the third harmonic from the initial degree-four frequency interval is a canonical first sparse support gap. The exact constant \(3/2\) quantitatively separates the sparse problem from the classical degree-two and degree-four constants \(\sqrt2\) and \(\sqrt3\), and the unique factorized extremizer supplies a reusable structural benchmark for sparse Carathéodory–Fejér problems. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a table recomputation.
